findings.title: Findings converge on the attribute-level coverage gate (D2-B)
findings.chosen: B: Keep D2-B and address Findings 4, 5, 6 individually.
findings.recommended: B: Keep D2-B and address Findings 4, 5, 6 individually.

findings.title: The timer drive has no synchronization contract
findings.chosen: Drive via service calls only; wait with timeout for each expected state; fix HA citation

findings.title: D1 doesn't say how collected states flow into conversion and the gates
findings.chosen: Handler appends raw dicts to one observed list; convert in test body; gates read the same list

findings.title: Attribute gate needs a derivation engine; a drive table could replace it
Attribute allowlist entries: stale-checked or not
findings.chosen: A: Stale-check domain entries only; attribute entries carry a reason and are not stale-checked. State this in D2.
findings.recommended: A: Stale-check domain entries only; attribute entries carry a reason and are not stale-checked. State this in D2.
findings.choice_reason: asked what stale-checked meant; agreed after explanation

findings.recommended: C: Accept as a known limitation

A bad helper block in the shared config surfaces indirectly
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation

findings.title: Under CI's invocation the registry holds test-module state classes, so the test errors on every run
findings.why_it_matters: models is built from the process-global registry, which pytest -m system with no path pollutes with unit-test state classes
findings.recommended: A: build `models` only from registry entries whose class file resolves under `PACKAGE_ROOT`, so the scope is the shipped catalog.
findings.chosen: A: build `models` only from registry entries whose class file resolves under `PACKAGE_ROOT`, so the scope is the shipped catalog.

findings.title: The drive isn't idempotent on the session-scoped HA, so `--reruns 2` replaces the real failure with a timeout
findings.why_it_matters: a rerun times out on helpers the first attempt already moved, and CI reports that instead of the real failure
findings.recommended: A: mark this test `flaky(reruns=0)` so its first failure is the one reported.
findings.chosen: A: mark this test `flaky(reruns=0)` so its first failure is the one reported.

findings.title: The hand-typed derivation can silently shrink, and nothing pins that it still covers timer
findings.why_it_matters: load_overrides returns {} on a missing directory, dropping timer/script/automation from the gate while the test stays green
findings.chosen: at the end of `hand_typed_domains`, assert a canary on the derived set before returning it

findings.title: Hand-written `wire_name`/type overrides in discovered domains escape the attribute gate
findings.why_it_matters: a wrong wire_name leaves the field None without failing conversion, the #3794 shape
findings.recommended: A: treat every attribute named in a discovered domain's `property_overrides` as hand-typed for the attribute gate.
findings.chosen: A: treat every attribute named in a discovered domain's `property_overrides` as hand-typed for the attribute gate.

findings.title: The release chain couples five entities to populate four attributes, and could be a linear drive
findings.why_it_matters: a second mechanism and an ordering invariant beside the step list, and the source of both races hit during the build
findings.recommended: A: replace the release chain with linear steps, confirmed by one live run.
findings.chosen: A: replace the release chain with linear steps, confirmed by one live run.

findings.title: The hand-written `todo` config entry couples the fixture to HA's storage schema, and TESTING.md overstates the duty it creates
findings.why_it_matters: a rejected entry surfaces as a todo domain-gate failure with no pointer, and the doc asks for minor_version upkeep that guards nothing
findings.recommended: A: keep the entry and correct TESTING.md to say the entry follows the pinned HA's schema and a `todo` domain-gate failure after a bump means it stopped loading.
findings.chosen: A: keep the entry and correct TESTING.md to say the entry follows the pinned HA's schema and a `todo` domain-gate failure after a bump means it stopped loading.

findings.title: The monthly HA bump has no pointer to this test's upkeep
findings.why_it_matters: the bumper first learns of a gate failure as a red CI after the commit is prepared
findings.recommended: A: extend SKILL.md's Phase 4 note to name `test_state_models.py`, how to run it locally, and its upkeep (stale `DOMAIN_ALLOWLIST` entries, new domains, the `todo` config entry).
findings.chosen: A: extend SKILL.md's Phase 4 note to name `test_state_models.py`, how to run it locally, and its upkeep (stale `DOMAIN_ALLOWLIST` entries, new domains, the `todo` config entry).

findings.title: A step's wait can be satisfied by a late or duplicate state from an earlier step
findings.why_it_matters: a late matching state could pass a step before its call took effect, failing misattributed on the attribute gate
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: a late duplicate state can satisfy a step's wait, surfacing as an attribute-gate failure rather than a named step.
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: a late duplicate state can satisfy a step's wait, surfacing as an attribute-gate failure rather than a named step.

findings.title: Fifteen 15s step waits can exceed the 120s pytest timeout, turning a named timeout into a thread dump
findings.why_it_matters: a uniformly slow runner dies at the harness timeout without naming the step
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: on a uniformly slow runner the test can hit pytest's 120s timeout and fail with a thread dump instead of a named step.
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: on a uniformly slow runner the test can hit pytest's 120s timeout and fail with a thread dump instead of a named step.

findings.title: `last_action` may appear before the script's trigger listener is attached
findings.why_it_matters: the release could race the script's trigger subscription; moot after the linear drive
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: the release can in principle race the script's trigger subscription, failing loudly as a timeout (moot if Finding 5's linear drive is adopted).
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: the release can in principle race the script's trigger subscription, failing loudly as a timeout (moot if Finding 5's linear drive is adopted).

findings.title: The recorder's step label is sometimes wrong
findings.why_it_matters: a late event can carry the next step's label in a failure message
